drivers_changed: Year-1 growth +0.2pp in every scenario (base 3.9 -> 4.1, bull 4.3 -> 4.5, bear 3.0 -> 3.2): revenue guidance midpoint raised 1.2% ($17.25B -> $17.45B), implied Q4-26 ~$4.35B (+5% YoY), volume drag improved to -0.6%. Sized so that base Oct-26..Sep-27 revenue (~$17.95B) sits ~1.1% above what the prior path implied for the same twelve months; not higher, because Q3's +2.1pp Environmental Solutions contribution includes lumpy project/PFAS work.

Year-1 EBITDA margin -0.2pp and year-2 -0.1pp in every scenario (base 31.3/31.5 -> 31.1/31.4; bull 31.5/31.9 -> 31.3/31.8; bear 31.0/30.7 -> 30.8/30.6): the raised guidance implies a FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin of ~31.9% vs ~32.1% before (revenue +$200M, EBITDA +$25M), and Q3 adjusted margin was 31.8% vs 32.8% on fuel, healthcare and the lapping of 2025 hurricane-recovery landfill volumes. Fuel and the event comp are transient, healthcare is not, so the cut fades by year 3 rather than persisting.
deliberately_unchanged: Growth years 2-10 (all scenarios): core price 5.3% and yield 2.9-3.4% are tracking the normalisation the path already assumed. Would move on FY2027 guidance (February 2027) showing yield below ~3% with volume still negative, or volume turning sustainably positive.

EBITDA margin years 3-10: one quarter of fuel/healthcare pressure does not reset the mature margin. Would move if FY2027 guidance shows adjusted margin flat or down on FY2026, or if PFAS leachate-treatment costs appear in operating expense.
D&A 11.0% and capex 11.2-11.4% of revenue: TTM 11.0% and 11.3%, in line.

Cash tax path 15% -> 22%: 9M-26 cash taxes were lower again ($122M), which argues the shelter persists, but the path deliberately does not perpetuate bonus depreciation. Would move on a change in the bonus-depreciation regime or a disclosed multi-year tax-credit purchase programme.
SBC path 0.35-0.36% of revenue: TTM 0.37% including withholding.

Scenario weights 20/55/25. The DC Circuit ruling upholding the PFOA/PFOS CERCLA designation without a passive-receiver exemption closes one route to relief, but the bear path already carries PFAS-driven margin compression and higher capex/closure spend, and no cost has been quantified or accrued. Would raise the bear weight on a proposed EPA landfill effluent guideline with costed leachate standards (expected ~2027), a PFAS accrual, or a named-defendant CERCLA action.
Buybacks ($5B 2027-2029 authorization): value-neutral in this model; share count stays flat at the current diluted figure.
Tuck-in M&A still excluded as NPV-neutral.
Historical CAGRs: full-year FY2022/FY2020 -> FY2025 basis, no new fiscal year.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (7.1%) is >30% below EPS 5yr CAGR (17.7%): EPS is lifted by buybacks (~3% of shares retired since FY2020), margin expansion and the FY2020 COVID trough base. Revenue CAGRs (7.1% 3yr / 10.3% 5yr, net-revenue basis) include the US Ecology acquisition (2022) and ~$1B/yr of tuck-ins; organic growth is ~4-5% (core price 5-6%, volume -1%). The DCF uses organic growth, not the selected equity CAGR, because M&A spend is not modelled.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr); unchanged in this update (no new fiscal year). Revenue from RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax (net). Owner FCF = OCF - capex - SBC. SBC is flat at ~$40-50M while FCF grew, so the owner-FCF CAGR is marginally ABOVE the reported one -- no hidden stock-comp funding of growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Republic compounds as a price-led oligopolist: 4-5% core price offsets -1% volume, organic revenue ~4-4.5% decaying to 3%, margins recover the fuel/healthcare dip seen in Q3-2026 and inch up to 32% on automation and the Polymer Centers, capex stays slightly above D&A. Tuck-in M&A continues but is assumed to earn its cost of capital, so it adds nothing to value here.
scenario_narratives.bull: Volume recovers alongside sticky 5%+ pricing; Environmental Solutions (PFAS-impacted material handling running ahead of plan) and Blue Polymers (food-grade rPET/HDPE with Ravago) grow faster than the core and command premium pricing from brand-owner recycled-content mandates; automation and EV fleet take EBITDA margin to ~33%. Organic growth 5-5.5% for four years.
scenario_narratives.bear: The pricing tailwind fades with inflation, municipal re-bids get competitive, PFAS regulation (CERCLA designation upheld; EPA landfill effluent guidelines expected ~2027) and labour/healthcare inflation take over a point off margin and push capex up, and cash taxes normalise as bonus-depreciation deferral unwinds. Organic growth settles at 2.5%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A wide-moat, low-variance compounder priced well above what its organic cash flows support. The owner-FCF DCF on organic growth and a 20x terminal cap values the equity far below the market, which pays roughly 30x EV/unlevered owner FCF -- i.e. the market capitalises the moat at a lower discount rate than 7.5%, expects ~$1B/yr of tuck-in M&A to earn well above its cost of capital, and since October has re-rated the shares ~20% on a guidance raise worth about 1% of house value. None of that is in the house base case.
key_risks_to_valuation: PFAS: the PFOA/PFOS CERCLA hazardous-substance designation was upheld on appeal without a landfill passive-receiver exemption; EPA landfill effluent guidelines (expected ~2027) could add leachate-treatment opex and closure/post-closure cost industry-wide; not quantified in filings
Terminal cap binds in base and bear (Gordon at 7.5%/3.0% is ~22.9x); value is sensitive to the cap and to WACC
M&A excluded: if tuck-ins earn well above WACC (plausible -- RSG buys at 6-8x EBITDA and synergises), the model understates value
Cash tax: persistence of bonus depreciation and tax-credit purchases could keep cash tax well below the 22% terminal rate
Margin: Q3-2026 adjusted EBITDA margin fell 1.0pp YoY; if fuel and healthcare inflation persist while core price keeps normalising, the base margin ramp to 32% is too generous
Leverage creep: ~$14B debt, and the $5B 2027-2029 buyback plus ~$1B/yr of M&A exceed free cash flow after dividends

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares Q3 2026 10-Q (306.479M; was 307.6M at Q2). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, and RSG's buybacks (TTM $1.13B) more than fund the flat count -- they shrink it, which this model treats as value-neutral capital return rather than per-share accretion. The new $5B 2027-2029 authorization is an authorization, not cash spent, and changes nothing here.
inputs.sbc_source: Q3-2026 10-Q statement of stockholders' equity, stock-based compensation net of dividend equivalents: 9M-2026 $38M (12+13+13) vs 9M-2025 $33M (13+11+9); FY2025 10-K $44M. TTM Sep-26 = 44 - 33 + 38 = $49M, plus ~$15M est. tax withheld on net-share settlement (Q1 'Issuances of common stock' treasury column -$19M is the withholding signature; no combined figure published). Immaterial at ~0.37% of revenue either way.
inputs.wacc_rationale: UNCHANGED from 2026-10-02. USD flows, USD rate. Rf 4.3% (10y UST), beta ~0.75 (defensive waste oligopoly), ERP 5.0% -> CoE ~8.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (interest $574M FY25 on ~$13.5B avg debt), after-tax ~3.6%; D/V ~16-18% at market -> ~7.2%. Rounded up to 7.5% for leverage creep from debt-funded M&A and PFAS liability uncertainty. Same WACC in all three scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario paths and weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (~$60M/yr) sits inside EBITDA as rent, so operating leases are NOT in net debt; finance leases are inside total_debt (10-Q 'Total Debt' carrying value $14,055M includes finance lease obligations) and their principal is therefore NOT deducted from flows. One treatment each, never both.
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-10-02 valuation for Q3-2026 results (10-Q, 30 Sep 2026) -- same model, anchors rolled one quarter, only year-1/year-2 growth and margin re-judged; see `reconciliation` and `update_notes`. MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing: US operating company -- a collection/transfer/landfill/recycling operator whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; not a REIT, bank, holdco or LIC). Adaptations file not needed (USD filer, USD quote, US GAAP leases, no NCI, SBC non-zero). FY0 is TTM to Sep-2026 so that year 1 (Oct-26..Sep-27) does not re-count 9M-2026 cash already in the September balance sheet. REVENUE BASIS: us-gaap RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax (FY25 $16,591M, the reported net revenue that guidance is framed on). TTM components: net revenue 17,238 (16,591 + 13,103 - 12,456); GAAP EBITDA (OI + D&A) 5,354 (31.1%); D&A 1,900 (11.0%); capex 1,940 (11.3%); OCF 4,500; asset-sale proceeds ~11; reported FCF = OCF - capex + proceeds = 2,571 (levered, after ~$500M cash interest; FY2026 adjusted FCF guided $2.565-2.585B). Owner FCF (last_fcf) = 2,571 - 64 = 2,507. The TTM figure fell ~$95M from June because Q3-26 OCF (1,139) was below Q3-25 (1,181) on working-capital timing and Q3 capex was heavier (495 vs 444); management raised full-year FCF guidance at the same time, so this is phasing, not a run-rate change. The engine's flows are UNLEVERED (EBIT x (1-t) + D&A - capex), so year-1 owner FCF (~$2.9B) sits above the levered TTM figure by roughly the after-tax interest bill; that is consistent, not a jump. EBITDA margin path is ex-SBC and NET of ~0.9pp of cash spent on landfill capping/closure/post-closure and environmental remediation that adjusted EBITDA excludes but OCF pays; the accrued closure/environmental liabilities are therefore charged in the flows and NOT put in the equity bridge. ACQUISITIONS: growth paths are ORGANIC (price minus volume) from year 2; tuck-in M&A ($1.43B FY25, ~$1.1B 9M-26) is treated as NPV-neutral capital deployment, so neither the acquired revenue nor the spend is modelled. Deals closed by September 2026 are in net debt, and their rollover revenue is in year 1. Buybacks: active repurchaser ($870M FY25, $856M 9M-26), so the flat count is funded with real cash. CASH TAX: FY25 cash taxes $206M and 9M-26 $122M (vs $166M 9M-25) remain depressed by 100% bonus depreciation and purchased renewable tax credits; book ETR ~17.5%. Modelled 15% ramping to 22% by year 8 -- not perpetuating the shelter, but not snapping to statutory either. PRICE: regular-session close, not an after-hours print; the stock is up ~20% since the prior valuation's price while the house value moved ~1%.

bear.narrative: Pricing power fades to ~CPI as disinflation resets escalators and WM/WCN/GFL compete harder for municipal bids; volume stays negative. The PFOA/PFOS CERCLA designation, now upheld on appeal with no passive-receiver exemption for landfills, forces leachate treatment and higher closure/post-closure spend (capex and cash closure costs up), fuel, healthcare and driver wage inflation compress EBITDA margin ~1.1pp from here, and bonus-depreciation deferral unwinds toward a full cash tax rate.

base.narrative: Core price runs 4-5% (CPI-linked municipal escalators plus open-market pricing in an oligopoly), volume flat to -1% as construction/industrial recovers slowly; EBITDA margin starts a touch lower on fuel and healthcare costs, then creeps ~0.9pp over five years from pricing over cost, route automation and Polymer Center contribution, then flat. Capex stays a touch above D&A for landfill cell build and fleet.

bull.narrative: Volume turns positive as housing/industrial activity recovers while core price holds 5%+; Blue Polymers and the Environmental Solutions (US Ecology, Shamrock) platform -- PFAS-related revenue already ahead of its $100M 2026 target -- grow above the core and lift mix; route optimisation, automated side-loaders and fleet electrification take EBITDA margin to ~33%. Bonus depreciation keeps cash tax low for longer.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged from 2026-10-02. Bear 20%: no solvency or refinancing risk (investment-grade, ~2.6x levered, laddered maturities) but PFAS is a live, industry-wide regulatory cost whose size is unknown; the appeals-court ruling confirms the exposure without quantifying it. Base 55%: the business is unusually predictable -- contracted, CPI-escalated, non-discretionary -- so the central path deserves more weight than the house 50%. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): the bull needs volume recovery AND margin expansion AND above-core growth in Polymers/Environmental Solutions at once, and Q3's margin compression is a reminder that the second leg is not yet visible.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
